questions.q: What are Azure ExpressRoute and AWS Direct Connect, fundamentally?
options: Dedicated, private physical network connections to the cloud that never touch the public internet
Faster versions of a site-to-site IPsec VPN tunnel
A VPN client used by individual remote employees
A feature of VNet peering that adds encryption
questions.explain: Both services provide a dedicated physical path to the cloud provider's network through a connectivity provider, bypassing the public internet entirely.

questions.q: Why doesn't ExpressRoute or Direct Connect need IPsec encryption configured the way a site-to-site VPN does?
options: The traffic never enters the shared public internet, so there's no shared public medium to encrypt against
IPsec is not supported on dedicated circuits
Encryption is handled automatically by the connectivity provider's billing system
Dedicated circuits are not capable of carrying encrypted traffic
questions.explain: Because the physical path is dedicated and private, there's no shared public medium in the middle that would require encryption the way a VPN tunnel over the internet does.

questions.q: Who provisions the physical cross-connect between an on-prem network and the cloud provider's edge router for ExpressRoute or Direct Connect?
options: A connectivity provider operating in an ExpressRoute location or Direct Connect location
The cloud provider ships a physical cable directly to the customer's office
No physical connection is required; it is entirely software-defined
The customer's internet service provider automatically provisions it
questions.explain: A telecom or colocation partner provides the physical cross-connect at a specific location, between the customer's network and a port on the cloud provider's edge router.

questions.q: In Azure, what is the peering type used to reach VNets over an ExpressRoute circuit?
options: Private Peering
Microsoft Peering
VNet Peering
Global Peering
questions.explain: Private Peering reaches VNets; Microsoft Peering is the separate peering type used to reach Microsoft 365 and other Microsoft services.

questions.q: Why do some regulated workloads specifically require ExpressRoute or Direct Connect instead of a VPN?
options: A compliance requirement that data never cross the public internet is satisfied by a dedicated circuit in a way encryption over the internet cannot satisfy
VPNs are not capable of being encrypted strongly enough for any compliance framework
Dedicated circuits are always cheaper than a VPN, which compliance frameworks require
Regulated workloads are legally prohibited from using any cloud connectivity
questions.explain: Some frameworks restrict data from crossing the public internet at all, even encrypted -- a requirement only a dedicated private circuit satisfies, not a VPN tunnel.
